status.nb: 8 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 33 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Rumbek, Juba og Abyei.

summary.en: Drone strikes in the disputed Abyei border region have killed dozens of civilians, with Sudanese forces blaming the RSF for the attacks. Communal clashes linked to cattle rustling in South Sudan have left at least ten people dead, and a violent incident at Akol Koor’s residence has led to a lawsuit before the judiciary. Two prisoners of war are scheduled to return home from Akobo, while the governor has urged General John Kenyi Latio to end fighting in Wonduruba. Riek Machar denied commanding the White Army in court and political parties and civil society signed a peace pledge ahead of the 2026 elections, according to reports.
summary.nb: Droneangrep i det omstridte grenseområdet Abyei har drept dusinvis av sivile, med sudanske styrker som legger skylden på RSF-militsen for angrepene. Kommunale sammenstøt knyttet til kyrtyveri i Sør-Sudan har etterlatt minst ti personer drept, og en voldelig hendelse i Akol Koor sin bolig har ført til en rettssak i domstolene. To krigsfanger er planlagt å bli sendt hjem fra Akobo, mens guvernøren har oppfordret general John Kenyi Latio til å avslutte kampene i Wonduruba. Riek Machar benektet å ha ledet White Army i retten, og politiske partier og sivilsamfunnet signerte et fredsløfte før valget i 2026, ifølge rapporter.

background.title: South Sudanese Civil War
background.extract: The South Sudanese Civil War was a multi-sided civil war in South Sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces. The civil war caused rampant human rights abuses, including forced displacement, ethnic massacres, and killings of journalists by various parties. Since the war's end, South Sudan has been governed by a coalition formed by leaders of the former warring factions, Salva Kiir Mayardit and Riek Machar. The country continues to recover from the war while experiencing ongoing and systemic ethnic violence.
